tally.headline: 4 of 12 gradeable claims held up, 4 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 2 points toward Houston Texans of the quote EdgeDesk captured at nflverse reference. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 45.9 sat 1.4 points above the captured total of 44.5.

closing_line.note: The line did not move between the captured quote and the close.

reasons: 4 claims held up, 4 held up in direction only and 2 did not. Parts of the read were right and parts were not.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — the spread result changed on the final score — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 0.5 and the game finished 5 the away way — 5.5 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A two-turnover edge
variance_markers.text: Buffalo Bills won the turnover battle by two, which is worth roughly a touchdown of scoreboard on average and is largely noise game to game.

variance_markers.label: The spread result changed on the final score
variance_markers.text: Before the last scoring play of the game the spread graded win; it finished loss. A number that moves on a score taken in the last minutes of a decided game is a scoreboard event, not a matchup one.

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning half held. There is something here to investigate without concluding the model is broken.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.
